It defines the system's boundaries, rules, and state maintenance during continuous operation. The execution chain (Tool Runtime → Permission Decision → sandbox → side effects) addresses "how to act and how to be constrained." It turns "the model wants to act" into "actually executing within controlled boundaries." The task chain (Task Runtime) addresses "how to run concurrently, how to persist, and how to report back." It lets background tasks, sub-agents, and remote execution share the same lifecycle management, without reinventing state management for each scenario. The extension layer (MCP/Skills/Plugins) is not a fourth isolated chain; it injects capabilities into the three main chains while adhering to "the outside can be lively, but the inside must converge"—external sources are uniformly translated into internal objects, and the system speaks only one language internally.
